newsitem.title: UK: Major says UK economic prospects best in long time.
newsitem.headline: Major says UK economic prospects best in long time.

text.p: Prime Minister John Major said promising figures on November retail sales, unemployment and average earnings meant British economic prospects were better than they had been for years.

"What we can see as we come to Christmas 1996 are perhaps the best economic prospects that we have seen across the United Kingdom for a very long time." he said after visiting a school in Northern Ireland.
"I don't think many people remember when the (economic) prospects were quite as rosy as they are at present," he told reporters in Dungannon, some 40 miles (65 km) outside Belfast.
"We now have to make sure that these rosy prospects are turned into future realities and I have every intention of ensuring that we do."
In the largest monthly fall for a quarter of a century, the November jobless total declined by a much larger than expected 95,800 to 1.93 million, or 6.9 percent of the workforce.
"They are not good, they are magnificent," Major said earlier of the jobless figures.

Evidence of a pre-Christmas shopping boom came in the form of retail sales up by 0.7 percent, a figure well above most experts' forecasts. Average earnings figures showed an increase of 4.0 percent in October, unchanged from the previous month.
"The growth in retail sales shows yet again that the economy is extremely bouyant," said Major.
